subject: english
question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

They come to me / yesterday to convince me / to settle the issue with my rival.

options.text: to settle the issue with my rival.

solution:
The correct answer is: **They come to me**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is the use of the present tense verb "**come**" in a past-time context (**yesterday**).
 
• When narrating an action that happened in the past, we need to use the past tense. So, "come" should be changed to "**came**" to match the past time frame.
 
• The correct sentence would be: '*They came to me yesterday to convince me to settle the issue with my rival.*'
 
• Now, the verb "came" is in the past tense, making it grammatically accurate for a past event (yesterday).

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.
